note1_unprunedStores.question: Is the page- or model-derived content in other guided tables (action proposals, clarification contexts, translation plans, preparation proofs, cached command responses, publication bases' initialContext.origin) in OBS-014 AC-3 scope, a disclosed residual, or a follow-up story?
note1_unprunedStores.ruling: A disclosed residual now, plus a follow-up story by @pm. It is NOT in OBS-014 scope, so @architect does not need to extend the AR-2 prune design for OBS-014.
note1_unprunedStores.consistencyWithX6: X6 put the never-published publication copies into AC-3 because they are equality-bound copies of the very columns AC-3 prunes. The V15 capture guards require observation = progress->'observation' and execution_evidence = progress->'executionEvidence'. Keeping them would make the AC-3 oracle 'pruned content is gone' false. The stores in this note are distinct records with their own integrity roles: the admission chain, association checks, single-assignment triggers, and command idempotency. They are not byte copies of a pruned column. Rule applied: an equality-bound copy of a pruned column falls in AC-3; any other content-bearing store becomes a disclosed residual with a follow-up, never dropped by omission. That is the X6 fallback form (a named residual in the AC-2 document and the OBS-010 compliance gate, plus a @pm follow-up).
whyNotInScope: AC-3's text names two columns. Extending it to six more tables would change the AC's meaning, which this brief excludes.
AR-2 did not trace these stores field by field, so no safe prune design exists. Each needs a V19/V20 relaxation of a V14 guard, and V12-V18 are frozen.
OBS-014 is InProgress, with V19 being authored in the S3 unit. Reopening AR-2 mid-flight would put the RK-2 roll-forward-together unit at risk.

note2_twoPolicySources.question: Learning reads the governed policy (OBS-014 AC-1) while replay reads the configured TrustedPolicy. Where does the follow-up go, and what is the interim disclosure?
note2_twoPolicySources.ruling: Unifying the two sources is a follow-up story for @pm (@architect first). It is not placed in OBS-009 or OBS-015. OBS-015 gets a narrow T0 ruling request for the one place the two sources meet inside a single session.
note2_twoPolicySources.whyNotOBS009: OBS-009 covers deployable topology, the real-model benchmark and live proof. A change to replay authorization semantics during the D-C benchmark would move the gate's baseline. OBS-009 AC-1 only carries the governed policy hash as process configuration.
note2_twoPolicySources.whyNotWholeInOBS015: Unification changes replay authorization (ObservedReplayPins, ObservedReplayAuthorizer, currentPolicyHash) for every published revision, including ordinary scheduled replay. AR-2g deliberately freezes that path, and it is outside incremental re-learn. OBS-011 is behaviour-neutral and post-release, so it is not a valid home either.
note2_twoPolicySources.obs015Touchpoint: In the AC-3 mixed-mode session, prefix replay and suffix learning run in one session, so a governed narrowing could allow a prefix origin that the suffix refuses. @architect rules at T0, before T3, on the authorising policy for the prefix, the hash recorded for the merged revision, and the closed refusal. @po takes no option.
note2_twoPolicySources.interimDisclosure: In guided-data-flow.md (governance section) and the OBS-010 AC-5 policy-administration runbook row: (1) governed origins must be a subset of the trusted origins, re-checked at every learning start, so governance narrows and never widens; (2) approving or narrowing a governed version changes no replay binding or verdict for existing revisions, so published revisions keep replaying on an origin that governance removed for as long as TrustedPolicy allows it; (3) replay is bounded by the platform TrustedPolicy alone. OBS-010 AC-4 carries one row naming the interim state and the follow-up.
